title: Translate PDF – English to Arabic and Back, Free, No Upload
description: Translate a PDF between English and Arabic in your browser and get an editable Word document, headings and pictures kept. Free, nothing is uploaded.
heading: Translate PDF
subtitle: Translate a PDF from English to Arabic or Arabic to English into an editable Word document; nothing is uploaded.
intro: Translate a PDF online without sending it anywhere: the text is read from each page, translated on your device by the same English–Arabic language models Firefox uses, and written into a Word document you can edit. Headings, lists and pictures stay where they were, and Arabic comes out right to left. Machine translation makes mistakes, so the result is a Word file you can fix, not a locked PDF. Your file never leaves your device.

features.title: Private
features.text: The translation runs in your own browser; neither the file nor its text is sent to a translation service.

features.title: Editable result
features.text: A Word document with headings, lists and pictures, so a wrong word is easy to fix.

features.title: Both directions
features.text: English to Arabic and Arabic to English, picked for you from the file's text.

steps.title: Choose your PDF
steps.text: Click Choose a file, or drop a PDF on the page.

steps.title: Check the direction
steps.text: English to Arabic or Arabic to English is chosen from the file's text; change it if needed.

steps.title: Translate
steps.text: Click Translate to Word. The first time, the language model loads once.

steps.title: Download
steps.text: Download the .docx file and open it in Word or any word processor.

handles: English to Arabic and Arabic to English.
Headings, paragraphs and bulleted lists, each translated as a whole.
Pictures, placed in the flow where they sat on the page.
Numbers and codes without letters, kept as they are.
limits: Machine translation makes mistakes, more so with names, terms and short fragments; check what matters before you share it.
The first translation loads the language model (about 25 MB) from this site; after that it works offline.
The layout is close, not exact: drawn shapes, colours and backgrounds are left out, and tables come out as lines with tab stops.
Scanned PDFs hold pictures of pages, so make them searchable with OCR PDF first.
Only English and Arabic for now.

faq.question: Is my file uploaded?
faq.answer: No. Your file is read, translated and written by your own browser, on your device, and is never sent anywhere. You can check it: open your browser's network panel while you use the tool and you will see no upload, only the language model loading from this site the first time.

faq.question: How good is the translation?
faq.answer: It is machine translation by the same English–Arabic models Firefox uses for its built-in translation. It gets the meaning of most sentences across but makes mistakes with names, terms and very short lines, which is why the result is an editable Word document.

faq.question: Why is the result a Word document and not a PDF?
faq.answer: Translated text is longer or shorter than the original, and Arabic reads the other way, so it would not fit the PDF's boxes. A Word document flows the text and lets you correct it. Word to PDF turns it back into a PDF.

faq.question: Does it work with scanned PDFs?
faq.answer: Not directly. A scanned PDF holds pictures of pages; run OCR PDF on it first to add its text, then translate it.

faq.question: Does it work offline?
faq.answer: Yes, after the first translation in each direction. The language model is loaded once from this site and kept by your browser. Install OpenAnyDoc as an app (Install app, at the bottom of the page) to open it like any other program.

faq.question: Which languages can it translate?
faq.answer: English to Arabic and Arabic to English. Other languages may come later.

faq.question: Is it really free?
faq.answer: Yes. There is no account, no watermark and no limit on how often you use it.

faq.question: How do I translate a PDF from English to Arabic?
faq.answer: Translate a PDF by reading its text, translating it and writing it into an editable document, because Arabic text does not fit the boxes of an English PDF. In OpenAnyDoc, choose the PDF and the direction, and the text is translated on your device into a Word document you can correct; the file is never uploaded.
